messages:
Maria: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a runbook for the compatibility bridge for the /generate response-envelope rename. wondering scope: gateway-side shim vs client polyfill? short thread to decide.
Sam: Gateway shim easiest short-term. single place to translate envelope->response for all tenants. low dev effort. :thumbsup:
Alan: Caveat: gateway adds per-request CPU and adds ~0.8ms median p50 on our p95 load tests. that matters for strict SLO customers.
Tanya: Also increases memory churn because we deserialize+re-serialize. on Dedicated that kills packing efficiency for batching. we should measure impact on tail latency under 80% GPU saturation.
Kevin: From model/ML side: some downstream evals assume the old envelope shape. if we short-circuit at gateway we can ensure any cached KV hits still return old shape, which is safer for eval stability.
Maria: Tradeoffs noted. Proposal: 1) Gateway shim for 12 weeks as emergency compatibility bridge, 2) opt-in tenant flag to enable new envelope, 3) client SDK polyfills in parallel + docs, 4) telemetry to detect migrated clients.
Sam: +1. Implementation note: add header X-RW-Compat: envelope=v1|v2; gateway rewrites when header absent to v1 for backwards compat.
Alan: Can we avoid full JSON parse in the hot path? maybe a streaming rewrite for the top-level key rename to limit CPU? e.g. sed-like transform on first 1kb. risky but faster.
Tanya: Streaming is fragile for nested changes. prefer fast json library (simdjson) in gateway binary. bench shows ~40% lower CPU than python parsing.
Kevin: How do we handle Private (on-prem) installs? they may not want gateway mutation in their control plane.
Maria: Good call — plan: default behavior per-deployment type:
- Hosted: gateway shim enabled by default with header override.
- Dedicated: shim optional; enable via tenant config.
- Private: ship a shim binary as an opt-in package + docs, default off.
Sam: Need telemetry events: compat.rewrite.count, compat.rewrite.latency_ms p50/p95, compat.client-header.count. Also emit tenant_id so we can target waves.
Alan: Add a circuit-breaker: if rewrite adds >5ms p95 or error rate >0.1% for 5m window, disable shim cluster-wide and flip to 503 + banner to migration dashboard.
Tanya: Ops runbook items:
- How to toggle tenant opt-in (console flag + API)
- How to roll back gateway changes (k8s rollout pause & rollback)
- Backpressure steps if rewrite causes batch blowups (reduce max batch size)
- Incidents play: notify runtime-oncall + infra oncall
Maria: Draft of rollout waves:
1) internal smoke (1 team)
2) 5 pilot tenants (opt-in) + telemetry check 48h
3) gradual 10% -> 30% -> 60% traffic waves over 7 days
4) optional global enable for hosted after 12 weeks then remove shim and require client upgrade
Kevin: Tests: add compatibility fuzz harness that generates both shapes and validates semantically equivalent outputs. add golden prompt set to make sure old envelopes still map.
Sam: Implementation checklist (short):
- gateway: add header handling, simdjson-based transformer (Alan/Tanya)
- console: tenant flag + UI (Product/Console)
- sdk: polyfill + release notes (DevEx)
- telemetry: metrics/events (Sam)
- tests: fuzz/golden (Kevin)
Maria: Owners agreed? Alan/Tanya -> gateway, Sam -> telemetry + runbook infra, Kevin -> tests, I'll coordinate waves and console story.
Alan: I'll prototype simdjson transformer by EOD Wed and post microbench numbers to this thread.
Tanya: I'll add a stress test job to staging that simulates 70% batching and GPU saturation. link once ready.
deploy-bot: deployment pipeline triggered by @Alan for branch feat/compat-transformer. build 2026.03.21-237 queued.
Maria: Great. Last note: include migration banner in console and a deprecation timeline in 8 weeks for SDK owners so they have time. I'll write the short public-facing note and share for review.
Sam: I'll sketch the dashboards (rewrite latency, tenant opt-in funnel) and post a PR for dashboard templates.
Maria: Thanks everyone — summarizing: gateway shim temporary, tenant opt-in, client polyfills, telemetry + circuit-breaker, rollout waves, owners noted. follow-ups: Alan bench, Tanya stress job, Sam dashboards, Kevin tests.
Alan: ack.
Kevin: ack.
Tanya: ack.
Maria: closing loop — will copy this into the RFC follow-up doc and mark owners.
